name: AMD MI355X air-cooled rack (2 servers)

sources.title: Glenn Lockwood: MI355X notes (quotes the AMD MI355X brochure)

summary: Standard air-cooled rack holding two 10U 8-GPU MI355X servers (16 GPUs), such as Supermicro's AS-A126GS-TNMR. Rack power is an estimate built from the GPU board power. Power is AC to server PSUs.

nominalPowerW.note: Per server: 8 x 1,400 W GPUs = 11.2 kW, 2 CPUs at up to 500 W = 1 kW, 19 heavy-duty fans about 1 kW at typical load, memory, NICs and drives about 0.8 kW, giving about 14 kW. Two servers.

peakPowerW.note: Nominal plus fans at full speed and GPU transients, about 15.5 kW per server. Bounded above by 4 x 6.6 kW active PSUs = 26.4 kW per server.

weightKg.note: 2 x 133 kg (Supermicro AS-A126GS-TNMR net weight) + about 140 kg empty 42U enclosure + about 60 kg PDUs, switch and cabling.

widthMm.note: Generic 42U enclosure, 600 mm wide by 1,200 mm deep by 2,000 mm tall; actual size depends on the enclosure vendor.

depthMm.note: Generic 42U enclosure, 600 mm wide by 1,200 mm deep by 2,000 mm tall; actual size depends on the enclosure vendor. The server chassis is 843 mm deep.

heightMm.note: Generic 42U enclosure, 600 mm wide by 1,200 mm deep by 2,000 mm tall; actual size depends on the enclosure vendor.

maxLiquidFraction.note: Air-cooled OAM modules with no cold plates: all heat goes to air. A rear-door heat exchanger moves it to water at the rack.

maxCoolantSupplyC.note: Not applicable: air-cooled servers have no liquid loop. Facility water limits come from the RDHx or air handler serving the rack.

capexUsd.note: No public price. Assumed about $25k to $30k per MI355X GPU plus about $60k to $80k per server for chassis, CPUs, memory and NICs, plus about $30k for enclosure and PDUs.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Shipping since the second half of 2025 from several OEMs. Assumed 8 to 16 weeks for a standard configuration.
